summary: Mali requires most visitors to obtain a visa, now applied for and paid online through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' consular portal, and the UK advises against all travel to the country. The ministry's visa check still waives the visa for most ECOWAS nationals despite Mali's January 2025 withdrawal from the bloc, but not for Cape Verde, Ghana, Liberia or Sierra Leone, and it answers that citizens of its Confederation of Sahel States partners Burkina Faso and Niger need no visa.

proofOfFunds.text: Mali's Law No. 04-058 of 25 November 2004 on the entry of foreigners, which the online visa application shows before the form, says every foreigner entering Mali must carry, besides the entry visa, documents on the purpose and conditions of the stay and, where applicable, on their means of subsistence and guarantees of repatriation. No amount is stated.

payments.text: Canada's travel advice says credit cards are rarely accepted outside a few major hotels, that access to ATMs is limited outside Bamako, and that exchange facilities are often slow.

safety.text: The UK advises against all travel to the whole of Mali. It says JNIM has implemented blockades on key routes in southern and western Mali, including around Bamako, targeting fuel trucks and enforcing checkpoints for travellers, that leaving by overland routes to neighbouring countries is too dangerous, and that there is a high threat of kidnapping across Mali, including in Bamako. Canada says Mali has been ruled by a military-led transitional government since the August 2020 coup.

bestTimeToVisit.text: Canada's travel advice describes three seasons: dry and cool from November to February, dry and hot from March to June, when temperatures can reach 45°C, and rainy from June to October, when seasonal flooding can hamper overland travel. Both Canada and the UK advise against all travel to Mali.

tips.text: The UK advises against all travel to the whole of Mali, including Bamako. It says terrorist attacks can occur at any time, that JNIM blockades target key routes, and that there is a high threat of kidnapping across the country.

Mali formally left ECOWAS in January 2025 together with Burkina Faso and Niger. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs' visa check still waives the visa for nationals of Benin, Côte d'Ivoire, Gambia, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Nigeria, Senegal and Togo, but asks those of Cape Verde, Ghana, Liberia and Sierra Leone to apply.

The UK Foreign Office says not to take pictures of military or government installations and to always ask permission before photographing local people; Canada says photographing military personnel and installations is prohibited.
Canada's travel advice says credit cards are rarely accepted outside a few major hotels and that ATM access is limited outside Bamako.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Mali?
faq.answer: Most nationalities do. The application and payment are made online through the Malian Ministry of Foreign Affairs' consular portal, and the entry permit is issued electronically. Most ECOWAS nationals are still exempt (Cape Verde, Ghana, Liberia and Sierra Leone are not), and the ministry's visa check also answers that citizens of Burkina Faso and Niger need no visa.

faq.question: Is Mali safe to visit?
faq.answer: No. The UK and Canadian governments both advise against all travel to Mali; Canada cites the threat of terrorism, kidnapping, banditry and fuel shortages.

faq.question: Can ECOWAS citizens still enter Mali visa-free?
faq.answer: Most can. Although Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger formally withdrew from ECOWAS in January 2025, the Malian Ministry of Foreign Affairs' visa check still tells nationals of Benin, Côte d'Ivoire, Gambia, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Nigeria, Senegal and Togo that they need no visa. Nationals of Cape Verde, Ghana, Liberia and Sierra Leone are told a visa is required.

faq.question: Can I get a visa on arrival in Mali?
faq.answer: No official source we could read offers a visa on arrival. Apply online before travel through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' consular portal (diplomatiemdc.gouv.ml), selecting the Malian embassy or consulate that covers your country of residence; the UK Foreign Office says the entry permit is issued electronically once approved, with no need to send documents to the embassy.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever vaccination for Mali?
faq.answer: Yes. The UK Foreign Office says you must have a certificate proving yellow fever vaccination to enter Mali.
